chief_complaint: gradual short-term memory loss and getting lost in familiar places
hpi_details: 75-year-old female is brought in by her son due to progressive memory loss over the past 3 years. She frequently repeats the same questions, forgets recent conversations, and recently got lost while driving to her local grocery store, a route she has driven for 20 years. Her ADLs are increasingly impaired.
ideas: thinks it might be related to alzheimer
concerns: worried about potential complications and long term recovery
expectations: wants complete diagnostic evaluation and treatment plan

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Alzheimer Dementia is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Plan for Alzheimer Dementia: Donepezil, Memantine, safety planning, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: gradual short-term memory loss and getting lost in familiar places

Key HPI features: Progressive 3-year short-term memory loss, repeated questions, forgotten recent conversations, and getting lost on a familiar route, with increasing impairment in activities of daily living.
Objective/Exam findings: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Alzheimer Dementia.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Alzheimer Dementia.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Vascular dementia without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Getting lost while driving.
management_principles: Plan for Alzheimer Dementia: Donepezil, Memantine, safety planning
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

source_refs.title: AAN Practice Guidelines for Neurological Disorders

reference_soap.subjective: 75F brought in by family for insidious, progressive short-term memory loss and spatial disorientation affecting daily functioning.
reference_soap.objective: Vitals normal. Alert, cooperative. Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) score is 19/30, losing points heavily on orientation to time, delayed recall (0/3), and intersecting pentagons.
reference_soap.assessment: Major Neurocognitive Disorder, probable Alzheimer Disease.
reference_soap.plan: Order non-contrast MRI brain to evaluate for hippocampal atrophy and rule out vascular/structural lesions. Check TSH, B12, and RPR to rule out reversible causes. Initiate trial of an acetylcholinesterase inhibitor (e.g., Donepezil). Refer for cognitive and driving safety evaluation.

learning_objectives: Recognize clinical presentation and diagnostic markers of Alzheimer Dementia
Select appropriate diagnostic workup for Alzheimer Dementia
Implement evidence-based management plan: Donepezil, Memantine, safety planning

teaching.one_liner: Progressive short-term memory loss and getting lost in familiar places from amyloid plaques and neurofibrillary tangles.

must_ask.say: Has she gotten lost in familiar places?
How many years has this progressed?
What worries you about her safety?
